title: The One Where Rachel Tells...

jokes.text: Ross denies owning a Speedo, then immediately says he'll go pack his 'regular, long bathing suit'
jokes.setup: Monica says she couldn't find Ross's Speedo while packing, implying he owns one
jokes.punchline: Ross denies it, then exits to pack his 'regular, long bathing suit' — a transparent euphemism that confirms he's embarrassed about it
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom denial-that-confirms joke. The 'regular, long bathing suit' phrasing is the key — it's specific enough to be funny. Ross's embarrassment is well characterized. Not groundbreaking but clean execution.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I packed for you, but I couldn't find your Speedo.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: That's because I don't own a Speedo.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, that's what I figured.

jokes.text: Monica, Phoebe, and Joey all claim to be the baby's aunt/uncle, with Monica asserting 'I'm the only one related by blood'
jokes.setup: Everyone enthusiastically claims they'll be the baby's aunt or uncle
jokes.punchline: Monica one-ups them all by pointing out she's the only one related by blood — delivered with a slight competitive edge
jokes.explanation: Monica's competitiveness is perfectly in character. The escalation from generic warmth to territorial blood-claim is a solid character beat. Mild laugh, well-integrated.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I don't own a Speedo. I have a regular, long bathing suit.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's just what you call it.

jokes.text: Chandler tells Joey about Rachel and Ross's baby — Joey reacts with exaggerated shock, then catches himself: 'Why am I talking like this?'
jokes.setup: Chandler reveals the pregnancy news to Joey, who explodes in over-the-top shock
jokes.punchline: Joey pauses and self-consciously asks 'Why am I talking like this?' — breaking the fourth wall on his own dramatic reaction
jokes.explanation: Joey's self-aware break is genuinely clever — he's doing a soap opera reaction and then noticing it himself. The joke works on two levels: his outsized emotional response AND the meta-commentary on it. Well-structured and character-specific to Joey's dramatic tendencies.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Wait, you guys... Joey's the only blood relative to the baby.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? No I'm not!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Yes you are. You're my half-brother.

jokes.text: Joey claims to be 'an excellent secret-keeper' and says he's kept 'all our secrets' — but won't name any because he's such a good secret-keeper
jokes.setup: Chandler says he didn't tell Joey the secret because Joey can't keep secrets
jokes.punchline: Joey insists he CAN keep secrets and proves it by... refusing to name the secrets he's kept, using the act of secrecy to avoid admitting he doesn't know any
jokes.explanation: The circular logic is beautifully Joey — he's simultaneously proving he can keep secrets and revealing he has nothing to keep secret. The 'You'll tell me later? / You already know' kicker is tight. Strong character-specific absurd logic.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, that's terrible! I mean, why would they do that? It's like the universe is conspiring against us, you know? It's all connected, like the chakras, and the energy, and... wait, am I doing that thing again where I talk like I'm in a soap opera?

jokes.text: 'You'll tell me later?' / 'You already know.'
jokes.setup: Joey is convinced there are secrets being kept from him
jokes.punchline: Chandler flatly informs him that he already knows whatever secrets there are — Joey's paranoia is pointless
jokes.explanation: Perfect button on the previous joke. Maximum economy — four words deflate Joey's entire paranoid spiral. Functions best as a tag to joke #4 rather than standalone.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I can keep secrets! I'm very good at keeping secrets.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Phoebe, you told everyone about my new apartment before I could tell them myself.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: That was different! I thought it was public information.

jokes.text: Phoebe suggests she and her partner should 'do something' since Monica/Chandler got married and Ross/Rachel are having a baby — her partner responds 'All in good time, my love. All in good time.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe observes the romantic milestone energy and suggests they should follow suit
jokes.punchline: Her partner's pompous, measured 'All in good time' — condescending and weirdly formal as a response to what could be a marriage hint
jokes.explanation: Mild joke — the pompous response is slightly funny but the partner isn't a developed character so it doesn't land with full force. Passable transition gag.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm great at keeping secrets. I haven't told anyone that Monica is—

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: What? I stopped myself. And I would never tell anybody that Ross—

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I know, I know. See? I'm keeping it in.

jokes.text: Shoot! I left my guitar in their apartment. Well, you can let me in later, right? / No, I don't have a key. They took mine to give to you. / What? They took mine to give to you. / Why would they take away our keys?
jokes.setup: Phoebe forgot her guitar; she assumes one of them has a spare key to Monica and Chandler's apartment.
jokes.punchline: Neither has a key — Monica and Chandler took each of their keys to give to the other, leaving both locked out.
jokes.explanation: Functional plot-comedy setup. The circular key-giving logic is mildly amusing but it's mainly a premise-establisher for the subplot.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Will you tell me the secrets later?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, you already know them, so I'm not really revealing anything.

jokes.text: Phoebe mentions that the last time she kept Monica's key, she broke a ketchup bottle and cleaned it with Monica's guest towels — 'Hey, I washed those.' / 'No, you didn't.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe defensively says they were trusted with keys before
jokes.punchline: The story of ketchup and guest towels + Phoebe's weak defense 'I washed those' getting instantly shot down
jokes.explanation: The specific detail of the ketchup/guest towels is good — Monica's obsession with her guest towels is established character lore. The quick denial is a clean button. Functional supporting comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: We should follow our friends' relationship milestones.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Well, that's a very interesting perspective, Phoebe. However, I believe we should establish our own timeline based on mutual understanding and personal readiness, rather than succumbing to social pressure or external benchmarks.

jokes.text: Maybe they don't trust us. / They let me keep my key the last time they were out of town. / The time you broke the ketchup bottle and cleaned it with Monica's guest towels?
jokes.setup: Joey defends his trustworthiness by noting he kept the key last time.
jokes.punchline: Phoebe immediately undercuts him by citing the specific incident that probably led to this — the ketchup-and-guest-towel disaster.
jokes.explanation: Specific details (ketchup bottle, Monica's sacred guest towels) make this land. Very Friends-esque — Monica's cleanliness obsession is a reliable comic engine.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, Mike, remember when you ate a sandwich over Monica's white couch and got mayo on it?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: That was one time!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Exactly. One time was enough for Monica to revoke your key privileges.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'Yeah, that didn't sound like me.'
jokes.setup: Joey calls out that Phoebe cleaned the ketchup mess with Monica's guest towels and didn't wash them
jokes.punchline: Phoebe blandly comments 'Yeah, that didn't sound like me' — a denial so low-energy it's effectively a confession
jokes.explanation: The deadpan self-distancing is very Phoebe. The delivery timing implied in the script is good — she's not protesting, she's just mildly puzzled by the story. Nice button.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: I do wash the towels!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No, you don't.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: You're right, I don't.

jokes.text: Joey calls the super to report a fake gas leak emergency — 'Oh, and bring garlic bread.'
jokes.setup: Joey fabricates a gas leak emergency to get into Monica's apartment so he can retrieve... Monica's chicken parm
jokes.punchline: The request for garlic bread as an addendum to an 'emergency' call perfectly reveals Joey's actual priority (food) while pretending to be safety-concerned
jokes.explanation: This is one of the episode's best Joey moments. The escalating absurdity — fake emergency → real food motivation → garlic bread request — is perfectly economical. 'Oh, and bring garlic bread' is a quotable kicker that could only be Joey. High character integration, maximum laughs per word.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: So what stuff do you have in the apartment?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Well, I've got my guitar, some books, my collection of vinyl records...

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: What about the most important thing?

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: My leftover lasagna in the fridge.

jokes.text: Ross laments that Monica and Chandler left without his pass to the 'Nassau Fossil and Natural History Museum' — 'There goes the honeymoon.'
jokes.setup: Ross discovers he's missed saying goodbye to Monica and Chandler
jokes.punchline: His actual concern is a museum pass — the nerdiest possible honeymoon priority, undercut by the earnest 'There goes the honeymoon'
jokes.explanation: Very Ross — the specificity of 'Nassau Fossil and Natural History Museum' is what makes this. His deadpan 'There goes the honeymoon' as if a museum pass is the whole point of the trip is perfectly in character. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, it's Joey Tribbiani in 4G. Yeah, I got an emergency here. My toilet's overflowing and there's water everywhere!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, yeah, it's bad. Oh, and hey, while you're coming up, could you grab me a sandwich? A turkey sandwich? Actually, make it roast beef.

jokes.text: Ross tells Gunther that he and Rachel slept together about a month ago, expecting shock — Gunther says 'And?' completely flat
jokes.setup: Ross confides to Gunther about sleeping with Rachel, dramatically framing it as a big revelation
jokes.punchline: Gunther's completely flat, unimpressed 'And?' — delivered as if this is old news / irrelevant
jokes.explanation: Gunther's obsession with Rachel is well-established, so his 'And?' has layers — either he knew, doesn't care, or is suppressing jealousy behind a flat affect. The deadpan one-word response does heavy lifting. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh no, I forgot my museum pass! We can't go on the honeymoon without it!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, it's our honeymoon.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I know, and it's going to be so romantic. The Natural History Museum has a new wing on Paleolithic tools. We can't miss that!

jokes.text: Ross: 'Wow, I thought you'd be a little more shocked.' Gunther pauses, then performs shocked: 'Oh, sorry. And?!'
jokes.setup: Gunther's underwhelming reaction prompts Ross to comment on it
jokes.punchline: Gunther performs a belated, clearly fake version of shock ('And?!') while still withholding any actual emotional investment
jokes.explanation: This escalation on the previous beat is very well constructed — Gunther pretends to course-correct but his 'And?!' still ends with the same indifference. The double beat makes this sequence stronger than either part alone. Great Gunther character work.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I slept with Rachel!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, I know.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You know?!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, everyone knows.

jokes.text: Ross concludes: 'Maybe I'm not the type of guy women can have just one night with. They always seem to want a little bit more. I should remember that.'
jokes.setup: Ross is still misreading why Rachel wants to talk to him — he thinks she wants to restart their romantic relationship
jokes.punchline: His completely deluded self-aggrandizing conclusion that women just can't resist him — delivered with sincere earnestness
jokes.explanation: Ross's oblivious self-flattery while the audience knows he's about to get pregnancy news creates good dramatic irony. The phrasing 'I should remember that' as a memo-to-self is appropriately pompous. Character-specific dramatic irony works well here.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You gotta be more shocked, man. Like this.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

jokes.text: Monica and Chandler see a couple kissing in line. Monica says 'Leave them alone, they're in love.' Chandler: 'I'm in love too. But in an orderly fashion.'
jokes.setup: Monica is charmed by the kissing couple blocking the airport line
jokes.punchline: Chandler's 'I'm in love too. But in an orderly fashion' — perfectly captures his personality: emotionally willing but procedurally frustrated
jokes.explanation: Very sharp Chandler line — the juxtaposition of 'I'm in love' (romantic) with 'in an orderly fashion' (bureaucratic) is funny and character-specific. Economy is excellent. This is exactly the kind of line Chandler was written to deliver.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You know what my problem is? I'm too good-looking. Women see me and they immediately think 'relationship,' not 'casual dating.' I mean, look at me. How could anyone just keep this as a fling?

jokes.text: Monica tells Chandler to 'grab my ass' as part of their honeymoon performance to get a free upgrade
jokes.setup: Monica and Chandler decide to perform honeymoon affection to get bumped to first class like the couple before them
jokes.punchline: Monica's very specific, transactional instruction to Chandler to grab her ass — the romance is entirely fake and goal-oriented
jokes.explanation: The gag of Monica reducing romance to a tactical maneuver is funny and character-appropriate. The bluntness of 'grab my ass' as an instruction gets a solid laugh. Part of the building running gag.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could they BE any more in the way?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Aww, that's sweet. They're in love.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, their love is blocking the line. I like my love orderly, with good lighting and comfortable seating.

jokes.text: Monica performs being in love with her new husband to get an upgrade, but the agent tells her all first-class is taken — that couple got the last two. 'See? If we'd gone around them like I said, she'd have given us those tickets!'
jokes.setup: Monica's attempt to get a first-class upgrade fails because the couple they were annoyed at got the last seats
jokes.punchline: Chandler's 'I told you so' — the same couple they debated going around has now taken their upgrade twice
jokes.explanation: Solid callback payoff. The running gag mechanics are working. 'Damn it!' energy from Chandler is good. Slightly repetitive since it's the same joke beat as #15 but with added irony.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Did you see that? They just got upgraded to first class! Why didn't we get upgraded?

jokes.text: Chandler asks the agent if 25J and K 'any chance those aren't together?' — implying he doesn't want to sit with Monica
jokes.setup: They've been assigned seats 25J and K (adjacent economy seats) on their honeymoon
jokes.punchline: Chandler asks if the seats might happen to be non-adjacent — a passive-aggressive comment about wanting space from his new wife on their honeymoon
jokes.explanation: The joke lands on the implied 'I need a break from Monica' subtext. Chandler's self-aware weariness about marriage on day one is funny. Brief but punchy.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: We should go to the hotel and complain about something so we can get upgraded.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: But we're already married.

jokes.text: Joey tells Phoebe he trusts her with his key — 'just as soon as they're done with it at the key-shining place'
jokes.setup: Phoebe points out that Joey trusts her with his key, implying Monica and Chandler are wrong not to
jokes.punchline: Joey reveals he doesn't actually have her key — it's at the fictional 'key-shining place' — a completely made-up excuse that he delivers with total sincerity
jokes.explanation: The 'key-shining place' is brilliantly absurd — entirely invented, delivered with Joey's complete earnestness, and it confirms that he ALSO doesn't trust Phoebe with his key while pretending to. The layered irony and the specific fake institution make this one of the episode's better comedy moments.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Okay, when he comes in, I want you to run up and kiss me like you mean it.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Not like you actually like me or anything, just... convincingly.

jokes.text: Treeger arrives with an enormous key ring, explaining that he uses it instead of his apartment key to avoid having to find the right key — but his logic is that by the time he found it, 'the whole place might have exploded'
jokes.setup: Joey calls for Treeger because there's supposedly a gas leak emergency
jokes.punchline: Treeger has a comically massive keyring and his logic for using it (even though it presumably makes finding keys harder) is perfectly inverted bureaucratic reasoning
jokes.explanation: The visual of the giant keyring is a decent sight gag. Treeger's circular logic about why the keyring is better than a regular key is mildly amusing but underwritten. Broad physical comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I told you we should go around! But no, you all had to go through the middle like some kind of herd of confused cattle.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Chandler, we didn't know there was going to be a—

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: A what? A disaster? A catastrophe? Because I predicted that! I literally said, 'This will end badly,' and you all looked at me like I was insane!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: We get it, Chandler.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Do you? Do you really? Because I'm not feeling the 'getting it.' I'm feeling a lot of not listening to Chandler, which is apparently the default setting for this group.

jokes.text: Treeger: 'If that happens at another building I manage, people will ask questions.'
jokes.setup: Treeger explains his urgency in responding to emergencies
jokes.punchline: The implication that there have been previous building explosions at properties he manages — calmly referenced as a known fact
jokes.explanation: Nicely dark throwaway gag. The casualness with which Treeger implies he's had buildings explode before is the whole joke. Good economy and a surprisingly dark edge for Friends.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So... are we even going to sit together?

jokes.text: After Treeger breaks down the door with his massive equipment, Phoebe observes: 'Well, we could have done that.'
jokes.setup: Joey and Phoebe called in professional help to get into the apartment, making it a big production
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's completely flat observation that they could have just done what Treeger did themselves undercuts the entire effort
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom button — the absurd lengths they went to rendered pointless by one flat observation. Economy is perfect (six words). Phoebe's breezy delivery is well-suited. Standard but clean.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: You can trust me with your key.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, I know I can. But I have to take it to this place... it's a key-shining place. They make your keys all shiny and new.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: A key-shining place?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, it's in Brooklyn. You wouldn't know it.

jokes.text: Monica and Chandler try to sneak into the first-class lounge. Monica whispers 'Just act like you belong' — then immediately shouts 'Oh, my God! Oranges!'
jokes.setup: Monica and Chandler are pretending to belong in the first-class lounge
jokes.punchline: Monica immediately blows their cover by screaming about oranges — her love of food overrides her ability to act cool
jokes.explanation: The speed of the setup-to-implosion is what makes this great. Monica gives the instruction and immediately violates it in the same breath. 'Oh, my God! Oranges!' is a great specific choice — not caviar or champagne, but *oranges*. Perfectly reveals her character under pressure.

dialogue.speaker: Superintendent Treeger
dialogue.line: Joey, why did you break down my door?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: There was a gas emergency! I didn't have time to find my keys.

dialogue.speaker: Superintendent Treeger
dialogue.line: So you just smashed through the door?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I was panicking! You know how long it takes to find keys?

jokes.text: Chandler tries to bluff his ticket number to the lounge guard — 'I have it memorized. It's 1A.' The guard asks him to move his thumb. He can't back down.
jokes.setup: Chandler attempts to pass off his economy ticket as first class by covering the seat number with his thumb
jokes.punchline: The guard asks him to move his thumb — Chandler doubles down and claims he has the number memorized as '1A', which is immediately exposed
jokes.explanation: Solid cringe comedy. Chandler's decision to double down rather than retreat is very true to the character. The escalating specificity of the lie ('I have it memorized. It's 1A.') is well-structured. Good cringe.

dialogue.speaker: Treeger
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, it's not the first time this has happened.

jokes.text: Guard says 'Sir, this isn't a first-class ticket, I'm sorry.' Chandler: 'Apology accepted. Excuse us.'
jokes.setup: Chandler has just been caught trying to bluff his way into the first-class lounge
jokes.punchline: He accepts the guard's apology as if he is the aggrieved party, then exits with dignity
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. Chandler flips the power dynamic entirely in four words — 'Apology accepted. Excuse us.' — turning total humiliation into a dignified exit. The brazenness is perfectly Chandler. High quotability, excellent economy, completely character-specific. Comparable to the 8.0 anchor benchmark.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You know, you could've just used a key.

jokes.text: Ross tells Rachel he knows why she's there — she doesn't want to restart their romance, he thinks she just wants 'one more time.' He monologues while she tries to tell him she's pregnant.
jokes.setup: Rachel has come to tell Ross she's pregnant with his baby
jokes.punchline: Ross completely misreads the situation and launches into a speech about not restarting their relationship — the audience knows the truth, adding painful dramatic irony
jokes.explanation: Good sustained cringe setup — Ross's confident misreading is very Ross, and the audience's knowledge makes every line land with extra irony. The extended nature dilutes individual punch but the sequence works as a whole.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, look at all this fruit!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Monica, don't—

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: There's a pineapple! An actual pineapple!

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Can I help you find something?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: We're not supposed to be here, are we?

jokes.text: I mean, look, that one night we had was fun and certainly passionate. But don't you think it's better if we just stay friends?
jokes.setup: Ross is letting Rachel down gently, believing she wants to restart their romance.
jokes.punchline: He is catastrophically misreading the situation — Rachel is there to tell him she's pregnant, not declare romantic feelings — so his entire 'let her down easy' speech is profound dramatic irony.
jokes.explanation: Good sustained cringe-irony. Ross's confident misreading extends for several beats, with Rachel's increasingly baffled 'What?' reactions adding to the discomfort-comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Can I see your tickets, please?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh, the tickets? Yeah, they're... they're in my other pants.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Sir, you're wearing pants.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Right, well these are my OTHER other pants. I have a lot of pants.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: I'm going to need to see some ID.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: ID? Sure! I'm... I'm actually the pilot. Captain... Chandler Bing. And this is my first-class seat right here. See? It has a massage chair. And caviar. And a... a hot tub.

jokes.text: Seriously, what?
jokes.setup: Ross has just finished his extended monologue about why they should 'just stay friends.'
jokes.punchline: Rachel's flat, bewildered 'Seriously, what?' — a reaction beat that lands as pure deflation of Ross's self-important speech.
jokes.explanation: Two words that demolish everything Ross just said. The 'Seriously' adds genuine exasperation to the standard 'what?' — perfect economy, well-earned from the cringe buildup.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: I'm so sorry, sir. Those tickets are counterfeit. You can't go in.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh, well, thank you for the apology. That really means a lot. I feel so much better now that you've said sorry. In fact, I'm going to frame that apology and hang it in my apartment right next to my fake tickets.

jokes.text: Ross, still misreading the situation, offers: 'You know what? If you want to, we can do it one more time. I mean, I'd be okay with that. In fact, I have some time right now.'
jokes.setup: Ross thinks Rachel came to restart their romantic relationship
jokes.punchline: His gracious offer to sleep with her again — including the casual 'I have some time right now' — is simultaneously self-important and oblivious
jokes.explanation: 'I have some time right now' is the best beat — the nonchalant scheduling of a generous romantic offer is very funny. Ross's unearned magnanimity is well-characterized. The cringe of the moment is working hard.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: It's like a seesaw, you know? Up and down, up and down...

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Sometimes you're on top, sometimes I'm on top...

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: And sometimes we both just jump off and there's this moment where nobody's on the seesaw and it's just... there.

jokes.text: Ross still hasn't responded. Rachel adds: 'And you're the father, by the way. But you got—' and then Ross remains catatonic.
jokes.setup: Ross hasn't responded to 'I'm pregnant'
jokes.punchline: Rachel has to add the additional clarification 'and you're the father' as a footnote, as if the first bomb wasn't enough — and he still doesn't move
jokes.explanation: The 'by the way' escalation on his continued non-response is well-structured. Each new piece of information delivered to a statue gets progressively funnier. Good escalation work.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, we need to talk.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh my God, yes! Yes, I know what this is about. Rachel, I'm so glad you brought this up because I have been wanting to tell you how I feel.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You do?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes! I'm in love with you. I have been for so long and I just couldn't hold it in anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross... what are you talking about?

jokes.text: Ross: 'We used a condom.' Rachel: 'I know. But you know, condoms only work, like, 97 percent of the time.' Ross: 'What?!' Rachel: 'What?!' Ross: 'Well, they should put that on the box!'
jokes.setup: Ross is confused about how the pregnancy happened given they used a condom
jokes.punchline: Rachel calmly explains the 97% effectiveness rate — both react with 'What?!' then Ross demands it be on the box
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's signature moments. The mirrored 'What?!' reactions are perfectly timed — Rachel's is a mimicked shock at his shock. 'Well, they should put that on the box!' is highly quotable and captures Ross's tendency to redirect personal problems into consumer complaints. Great escalation setup.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I know you're still in love with me.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm married.

jokes.text: 'They do.' / 'No, they don't!' — beat — 'Well, they should put it in huge block letters!'
jokes.setup: Ross insists the condom warning should be on the box
jokes.punchline: Rachel confirms it IS on the box, Ross denies it, then immediately escalates to demanding it in 'huge block letters' — not retreating but doubling down
jokes.explanation: This is the episode's best joke. The escalation from 'it should be on the box' → 'they do' → 'no, they don't!' → 'HUGE BLOCK LETTERS' is perfectly constructed. Ross's refusal to absorb his error and instead escalate the complaint is brilliant character writing. The 'huge block letters' specificity is what seals it. High quotability, strong rewatch value, could only be Ross.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm pregnant.

jokes.text: Well, they should put it in huge block letters!
jokes.setup: Rachel confirms the information is on the box; Ross denied it.
jokes.punchline: Ross concedes — sort of — by upgrading his complaint from 'put it on the box' to 'put it in HUGE BLOCK LETTERS.' The escalation substitutes for an admission of being wrong.
jokes.explanation: The escalation from 'on the box' to 'HUGE BLOCK LETTERS' is a beautiful comedic move — Ross can't admit he was wrong so he shifts the goalposts to a more extreme position. The specificity of 'huge block letters' is very funny. This is the best beat in a great three-joke run.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. Only 97% effective? That's not good enough! I mean, what if I bought a parachute that was only 97% effective? I'd be very upset!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So why is it okay for condoms?

jokes.text: Ross: 'I'm indignant as a consumer!'
jokes.setup: Rachel tells Ross to forget about the condoms
jokes.punchline: 'I'm indignant as a consumer!' — Ross reframes his emotional freakout as a consumer advocacy position
jokes.explanation: Four words that perfectly crystallize Ross's character: when overwhelmed by emotion, he intellectualizes and displaces. 'Indignant as a consumer' is a perfect phrase — formal, pompous, and completely wrong for the situation. Very high quotability. This line alone would make a writer's room proud. Approaches the 8.0 anchor in quality.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: They don't put a warning on the box!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Yes, they do. It says right on there: 'Ninety-seven percent effective.'

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not a warning!

jokes.text: Ross: 'In fact, I wanna talk... to the president of the condom company.' Then: 'Yeah, I'll press one!'
jokes.setup: Ross's consumer outrage continues to escalate
jokes.punchline: He announces his intention to call the condom company president, then immediately self-soothes with 'Yeah, I'll press one' — as if navigating a phone tree is a war cry
jokes.explanation: 'Yeah, I'll press one!' is the perfect button — it makes the elaborate fantasy of confronting the condom company president immediately mundane and bureaucratic. The specific detail of phone tree navigation is inspired. This whole sequence (jokes 30-33) is the comedic centerpiece of the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: It says 'Some Assembly Required' on the box, but I've been working on this for three hours!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: They need bigger warnings. Like, 'WARNING: This will destroy your will to live' or 'CAUTION: You will question every decision that led you here.'

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: And there should be a picture of a man crying. Just a grown man, tears streaming down his face, holding a mysterious Allen wrench.

jokes.text: Joey and Phoebe try to explain the broken door to the building super by saying Monica and Chandler 'don't have any kids of their own... and this door was like a child to them.'
jokes.setup: Joey/Phoebe need to explain why the door was broken down without revealing the real reason
jokes.punchline: Joey's explanation that the door was 'like a child' to Monica and Chandler — both deeply revealing of his own thinking and completely unconvincing as a cover story
jokes.explanation: The 'door as child' metaphor is strange enough to get a laugh. Character-appropriate for Joey's odd logic. Not a standout but functional absurdist comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Can we please just move past the condom discussion?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh sure, yeah. I've actually forgotten all about them since they don't work anyway.

jokes.text: Treeger reveals the door repair will be an all-day job, forcing him to cancel his yoga class — then asks Ross to tell 'Jasmine' he can't make it
jokes.setup: Treeger is explaining the damage while trying to manage his personal schedule
jokes.punchline: The reveal that this large, gruff super does yoga — with a specific instructor named Jasmine — is an unexpected character detail played completely straight
jokes.explanation: Mild subversion of Treeger's tough-guy image. The specificity of 'Jasmine' makes it slightly funnier than a generic yoga joke. Light but serviceable.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You seem freaked out.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I'm not freaked out. I'm just... exercising my right as a consumer to express my dissatisfaction with a product or service.

jokes.text: Joey reacts to being told Rachel and Ross slept together AND Rachel is pregnant: 'Holy mother of God!' Phoebe: 'Oh, my God, I can't believe that!' Joey: 'With my child.' Phoebe: 'That is brand-new information!'
jokes.setup: Ross reveals Rachel is pregnant with his child
jokes.punchline: Joey's 'With my child' misdirect (suggesting he thinks it might be his) triggers Phoebe's perfect 'That is brand-new information!' — she was shocked about the pregnancy, now she has a whole new dimension
jokes.explanation: 'That is brand-new information!' is a sharp reaction line from Phoebe. The misdirect of Joey's 'with my child' — which makes it briefly sound like he's the father — is a quick but effective comic beat. Phoebe's response is perfectly calibrated. Good pair of lines.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I want to speak to a manager.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Actually, you know what? I want to speak to the manager's manager.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: In fact, I want to speak to whoever runs this entire operation. I want the CEO. I want the president of the company on the phone right now!

jokes.text: Ross admits he didn't handle Rachel's news well. 'What'd you say to her?' / 'Nothing. But the complaint department at the condom company got an earful.'
jokes.setup: Joey and Phoebe ask how Ross responded to Rachel's pregnancy announcement
jokes.punchline: Ross reveals he said nothing to Rachel but made a complaint call — the callback to the condom company bit lands with fresh absurdity
jokes.explanation: Strong callback — 'the complaint department at the condom company got an earful' recontextualizes the earlier scene perfectly. The fact that he abandoned the actual important conversation to make a consumer complaint is both funny and sad. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes, hello, I'd like to speak to someone about a defective condom... No, I don't want to press 1 for English, I'm already speaking English!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Look, I don't have time for this menu system. This is urgent!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, I will NOT hold. Do you have any idea what's at stake here?!

jokes.text: Joey reacts to the 97% condom statistic: 'So, like, 3 percent of the time, they don't even work? They should put that on the box!' — Phoebe: 'Evidently, they do.' Joey: 'What?!'
jokes.setup: Joey learns about the condom statistic for the first time
jokes.punchline: Joey has the exact same reaction Ross had — including the 'they should put that on the box' line — and gets the same answer
jokes.explanation: Smart running gag — the same joke beat works again because it's Joey independently arriving at the identical complaint. The mirroring of Ross's reaction validates the original joke while adding a new layer. Phoebe's calm 'Evidently, they do' as the already-established answer makes it even better. Good running gag mechanics.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Mr. Treeger, please don't tell Monica and Chandler about the door.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Treeger
dialogue.line: Why not?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Because they're gonna kill me! Look, what if we just don't say anything? It'll be like it never happened.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Treeger
dialogue.line: The door's completely destroyed, Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I know, I know. But think about it from the door's perspective. It's confused, it's scared... it's in a lot of pain.

jokes.text: Evidently, they do. / What?! / Well, I'll be.
jokes.setup: Joey/Phoebe says 'They should put that on the box!' — Ross corrects them.
jokes.punchline: The same exchange Ross had with Rachel plays out again — with the new character's 'Well, I'll be.' as the final button, an even more understated acceptance than Ross's denial.
jokes.explanation: 'Well, I'll be.' is a wonderfully understated acceptance — funnier than Ross's denial because it's so calm and resigned. Good running gag closer.

dialogue.speaker: Treeger
dialogue.line: Yeah, I do yoga. You got a problem with that?

dialogue.speaker: Treeger
dialogue.line: It's for flexibility and inner peace, alright?

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'Well, I'll be.'
jokes.setup: Joey is shocked that the condom warning is on the box
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's completely flat, grandmotherly 'Well, I'll be' — as if this is a minor curiosity rather than news that upended two people's lives
jokes.explanation: Three words that perfectly button the running gag. Phoebe's breezy underreaction is characteristically odd. Maximum economy. Works as a tag.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh my God! The door!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? What's wrong with the door?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What's wrong with it?! It's completely destroyed!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: So you think the landlord's gonna notice?

jokes.text: Monica and Chandler arrive at the hotel and discover the other couple has gotten the honeymoon suite. Monica: 'No! You have been screwing us all day!'
jokes.setup: The couple who got first class now gets the honeymoon suite ahead of Monica and Chandler
jokes.punchline: Monica's explosive 'You have been screwing us all day!' directed at the other couple — dramatic escalation of her growing rage
jokes.explanation: Monica's competitive fury is well-deployed here. The running gag has built enough momentum that this explosion is satisfying. The specific 'all day' accounting of their losses is good. Solid running gag payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Rachel's pregnant.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa! Rachel's pregnant?!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Joey, you knew that.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, but I didn't know that *you* knew that I knew that.

jokes.text: The other couple: 'Who are you?' Monica: 'We're you. Just 10 seconds later!'
jokes.setup: The other couple is confused why Monica and Chandler are angry at them
jokes.punchline: 'We're you. Just 10 seconds later!' — Monica identifies them as alternate-timeline versions who made slightly worse choices
jokes.explanation: 'We're you. Just 10 seconds later.' is a genuinely funny and quotable line. Monica's identification of the structural problem — timing — is sharp. Good economy and a memorable framing.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You knew about this the whole time, didn't you?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I may have heard some things.

jokes.text: The other couple offers to give up the suite: 'We don't care about where we stay. We're here to celebrate our love. We don't have to get free stuff. We just want to be together.' Monica and Chandler: 'We need the stuff.'
jokes.setup: The generous other couple offers to give up the honeymoon suite
jokes.punchline: Monica and Chandler's flat 'We need the stuff' — cutting through any pretense of romantic motivation to admit pure material desire
jokes.explanation: 'We need the stuff' is a great line — brutally honest, anti-romantic, and perfectly Monica. The contrast with the other couple's sincerity makes it land harder. Very quotable. Economy is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I called the condom company to complain about a defective product instead of being there for Rachel.

jokes.text: Joey calls Monica to report a fake gas leak. Chandler: 'Joey smells gas. What else is new?'
jokes.setup: Monica receives a call that Joey smells gas coming from her apartment
jokes.punchline: Chandler's 'What else is new?' — a dismissive joke implying Joey has digestive issues, delivered while they're supposed to be on a romantic honeymoon call
jokes.explanation: Quick flatulence joke dressed up as a Chandler quip. The gas/Joey association is a cheap joke type but Chandler's delivery saves it. Light laugh, standard sitcom territory.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, so condoms don't work like 100% of the time?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, they're about 97% effective.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh, so like the same odds as the box saying 'one size fits all'?

jokes.text: Monica tells Joey to break down the door. Joey: 'You sure you want this?' Monica: 'Yes!' / (second time, joke #44b) Monica: 'No, I want you to just wait for the place to blow up.'
jokes.setup: Joey hesitates before breaking down Monica's door and keeps asking for confirmation
jokes.punchline: Monica's sarcastic 'No, I want you to just wait for the place to blow up' — exasperated deadpan in response to his second round of questioning
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom sarcasm, Monica's exasperation is well-characterized. The 'wait for the place to blow up' response is a solid ironic line but fairly standard. Functional.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Why does it say 'Fragile' on the box? There's nothing fragile in there!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: That's because it says 'Fragile,' not 'Handle with care.' Fragile means it breaks easily.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, what? I've been throwing these boxes around for twenty minutes!

jokes.text: How? I guess I could break down your door. / Yeah, do that. / And you won't blame us for any damage? / No. / You sure you want this? / No, I want you to just wait for the place to blow up.
jokes.setup: Joey proposes breaking down Monica's door (a second time).
jokes.punchline: Monica's sarcastic 'No, I want you to just wait for the place to blow up' — the sarcasm perfectly calibrated for someone who has accepted the absurdity of the situation.
jokes.explanation: Functional sarcasm joke. Monica's exasperated acceptance of a ridiculous situation is in character, though the joke itself is fairly standard.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I was wrong. I accept that. Moving on.

jokes.text: Rachel in the OB-GYN chair: 'If I said I was [comfortable], would you judge me?'
jokes.setup: Ross asks Rachel if she's comfortable in the OB-GYN examination chair
jokes.punchline: Rachel's self-aware admission that she actually finds the medical chair comfortable — and her worry about being judged for it
jokes.explanation: Light but charming — Rachel's vanity/self-consciousness is well-integrated. The implication that she's comfortable in a medical stirrup chair is odd enough to get a small laugh. Nice character beat.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No! No, we don't want the honeymoon suite! We don't want anything from you! We just want to go to our room, pack our bags, and get out of here!

jokes.text: Ross looks at the OB-GYN examination table: 'Oh, man, I swear, if they sold these at Pottery Barn...'
jokes.setup: Ross is sitting with Rachel in the OB-GYN office, trying to lighten the mood
jokes.punchline: His admiration for the medical table as potential home furniture — the Pottery Barn reference implies he genuinely would buy one
jokes.explanation: Good light joke — the Pottery Barn reference is period-specific and the idea of buying a gynecological examination table as home furniture is nicely absurd. The incomplete sentence 'I swear, if they sold these...' leaves the conclusion implied, which is a smart economy choice.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Excuse me, but we booked this honeymoon suite first!

dialogue.speaker: Other woman
dialogue.line: Actually, we got married yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Other man
dialogue.line: So technically, we're on our honeymoon right now.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, so are we!

dialogue.speaker: Other woman
dialogue.line: Yeah, but ours just started.

jokes.text: Ross apologizes to Rachel while she's on the examination table. She says: 'Can you stay up near my head?' — then he keeps drifting toward the wrong end.
jokes.setup: Ross apologizes to Rachel while she's in the examination position
jokes.punchline: Rachel's repeated corrections of Ross's position — 'Head, Ross! Head, Ross!' — while he keeps wandering toward the wrong end of the table during his heartfelt speech
jokes.explanation: Good running physical gag — Ross's apology speech being repeatedly interrupted by Rachel's directional corrections is funny cringe comedy. The juxtaposition of emotional moment with practical embarrassment is a classic sitcom structure. 'Head, Ross! Head, Ross!' is a solid recurring beat.

jokes.text: Ross suggests they should get married. Rachel: 'Married? / 'Well, yeah, I think we should get married.' / 'Because that's your answer to everything?'
jokes.setup: Ross lists all the pregnancy-related things he'll help with, then proposes marriage
jokes.punchline: Rachel's 'Because that's your answer to everything?' — referencing Ross's history of impulsive marriage proposals
jokes.explanation: Strong meta-character joke — Rachel's reference to Ross's multiple previous marriages/proposals is funny because it's true (he'd been married three times). 'Because that's your answer to everything?' has real bite and is well-integrated into their relationship history.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: We need to think about our future. A house, investments, security.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, we can't just wing it like some people.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You know what Mike and I do? We just look into each other's eyes and feel grateful for the moment.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Life's about connection, not things.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Right, but what about when you get older and—

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: As long as we have each other, that's enough.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: That's... that's really nice, actually.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: So we're the materialistic ones now?

jokes.text: Ross: 'You can't even eat alone in a restaurant.' Rachel: 'What?!'
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to argue Rachel can't handle parenthood alone
jokes.punchline: His specific evidence is that she can't eat alone in a restaurant — a surprisingly petty and non-sequitur argument in a serious conversation
jokes.explanation: The specificity of 'eat alone in a restaurant' as proof of Rachel's incapability is funny precisely because it's such a strange metric. The escalating absurdity of their argument while in a gynecologist's office is well-constructed.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's beautiful. I want that. I want someone to say that to me. But I also want a really nice apartment in Manhattan, and clothes, and I want to be able to go out to dinner whenever I want. So, you know, ideally I'd like both.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'If you can't eat by yourself, how do you expect to have a baby by yourself?' Ross: 'I can too eat by myself!' Rachel: 'When have you ever?' Ross: 'When certain people leave the table and I am not finished!'
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel's serious conversation about parenthood devolves into an argument about solo restaurant dining
jokes.punchline: Their spiraling restaurant argument has them both simultaneously defending their dining independence as proof of parental fitness
jokes.explanation: The escalation of an existential parenthood argument into a petty restaurant dining dispute is good sustained comedy. 'When certain people leave the table and I am not finished!' is a very specific grievance with a good specific cadence. Character dynamics feel authentic.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey Chandler, there's a gas leak in my apartment!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, that's just you.

jokes.text: Ross: 'Well, certain other people take two hours to eat a bowl of soup!' Rachel: 'Oh, please. You inhale your food.' Ross: 'I grew up with Monica. If you didn't eat fast, you didn't eat!'
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel continue their absurd restaurant dining argument
jokes.punchline: Ross's 'I grew up with Monica. If you didn't eat fast, you didn't eat!' — introducing Monica as the source of his food-speed issues and a spot-on character callback
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's funniest lines — 'If you didn't eat fast, you didn't eat!' is a perfect Monica joke delivered through Ross. It deepens both characters simultaneously, is completely believable in the show's world, and delivers a big laugh. Strong character integration and quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, yeah, I'm still here. No, everything's fine. Why? Oh, that? That's just... that's just the radiator. Yeah, it does that. No, the ceiling's supposed to be like that. Look, I gotta go. Gotta go!

jokes.text: Dr. Long enters mid-argument. Rachel introduces Ross: 'This is Ross. He is the father. But not the husband, because, evidently, she can do this alone.'
jokes.setup: The doctor enters while Ross and Rachel are mid-argument
jokes.punchline: Ross's bitter, passive-aggressive introduction of himself to the doctor — summarizing the entire fight in one pointed aside
jokes.explanation: Ross's public airing of their private argument to a stranger is a good cringe beat. 'But not the husband, because, evidently, she can do this alone' has a sulking quality that's very Ross. Good character moment.

dialogue.speaker: Nurse
dialogue.line: Are you comfortable?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, no. I mean, how comfortable can you be with a man you just met having his hands all over your... you know.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Why [can't] you admit you need me?' Ross: 'I need you to stay near my head!'
jokes.setup: Rachel asks why Ross won't admit she needs him
jokes.punchline: Ross repurposes the question to mean his physical location — 'I need you to stay near my head' — which both deflects the emotional question and continues the physical gag
jokes.explanation: Clever double-meaning — Rachel's emotional question gets a literal answer that's also a callback to the physical gag. The pivot is fast and clean. Good economy and structure.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, this monitor is so cool! Do you think they sell these at Design Within Reach?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: And these IV stands? Very minimalist. Very now.

jokes.text: They see the sonogram. Ross says 'I see it.' Then quietly to Phoebe later: 'I lied. I didn't want her to think I was a terrible mother.' Wait — 'I can't even see my own baby!'
jokes.setup: The doctor shows them the baby on the sonogram screen
jokes.punchline: Ross pretends to see it immediately, then confesses he can't — and his reasoning is that he didn't want Rachel to 'think I was a terrible mother' (saying 'mother' instead of 'father')
jokes.explanation: Ross saying 'terrible mother' instead of 'terrible father' is a nice slip that reveals his anxiety about gender roles and parenting anxiety. The base joke of not being able to see the baby on the sonogram is universally relatable. Good emotional grounding for a laugh.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Rachel, I'm so sorry about what I said. I feel terrible.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, you can apologize, but you're going to have to do it from over there. I'm not exactly in a position to move right now.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Right, of course. I just wanted you to know—

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Actually, if you're going to keep talking, could you at least stand where I can see you? This angle is not doing you any favors.

jokes.text: Rachel finally sees the baby. She points it out again: 'Do you really [see it]?' Rachel: 'No, I don't see it!'
jokes.setup: Ross points out the baby on the sonogram and Rachel claims to see it
jokes.punchline: Rachel immediately admits she STILL can't see it — the same joke beat as Ross's admission but now they're both blind to their own baby
jokes.explanation: Good running gag payoff — both parents can't see the baby. The escalation of two separate admissions of blindness is funny. The 'No, I don't see it!' after claiming she did is a solid button.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, you need to stay still for the doctor!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, no, no — to the left. Your other left!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay, good boy. Good boy. Now sit. Sit!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Who's a good patient? Who's a good patient? You are!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No treats until after the exam, Ross!

jokes.text: Ross guides Rachel: 'You see this tiny thing that looks like a peanut?' / 'Yeah.' / 'Sweetie, that's it.' / 'That's it?' / 'Well, I saw that.'
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to help Rachel see the baby on the sonogram
jokes.punchline: After all the drama of not being able to see it, Ross's 'Well, I saw that' is a deadpan admittance that he could only see it because it was described as looking like a peanut
jokes.explanation: Button on the sonogram gag. Ross's 'Well, I saw that' is a neat pivot — he's defended by the peanut description while Rachel realizes she was looking at the wrong thing. Clean ending to the running gag.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So we need to start thinking about the nursery, and daycare, and of course the wedding—

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa. Wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I mean... for when we get married.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, we're not getting married.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh. Right. Yeah, I knew that.

jokes.text: Joey wonders how bad he wants one of Monica's turkey pot pies — weighing it against the risk of breaking into the newly secured apartment
jokes.setup: The apartment is now locked up with a new door
jokes.punchline: Joey's serious risk/reward calculation is entirely about the food — no other consideration matters
jokes.explanation: Callback to Joey's food motivation — now it's turkey pot pie. The fact that he frames it as a serious moral/risk calculation is very Joey. Light closing gag.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Wait, wait. Every time something goes wrong in your life, you propose to someone?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not true!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You proposed to Emily, you proposed to Rachel, you proposed to Bonnie...

jokes.text: The group looks at the sonogram photo. 'I don't see the baby. Where is it?' / 'Oh, no, I know. I couldn't see it either at first. But it's right—' / 'Ross, I lost it again.'
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel show the group the sonogram photo
jokes.punchline: The whole group can't see the baby — and Rachel loses it again even after having been shown — extending the running gag to a full ensemble moment
jokes.explanation: Perfect episode-closing running gag. 'Ross, I lost it again' is a great final beat — the fact that Rachel still can't see her own baby after being shown multiple times makes it funnier. The ensemble joining the confusion extends the joke organically.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You can't handle single parenthood. You don't even know how to make a proper meal. You'd probably feed the baby takeout every night.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: That is not true! I'm perfectly capable of—

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Rachel, last week you microwaved a salad.

jokes.text: Joey shows the group Rachel's sonogram: 'Show them the picture of your uterus.'
jokes.setup: The group wants to see the sonogram photo
jokes.punchline: Joey's characterization of it as 'a picture of your uterus' rather than 'a picture of your baby' — tone-deaf but technically not wrong
jokes.explanation: Joey's medically accurate but emotionally oblivious description of the sonogram. It's very Joey — he's not being insensitive, he just literally sees an image of a uterus. Mild laugh, good character moment.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I don't need a man to take care of me. I'm completely independent.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh yeah? Name one thing you've done completely on your own.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I... I got my own apartment!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Your father pays your rent.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, I bought my own furniture!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Monica helped you pick it out and Chandler carried it up the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay, fine. But I got myself this job!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You asked Monica's boss for it at Thanksgiving.

jokes.text: I don't see the baby. Where is it? / Oh, no, I know. I couldn't see it either at first. But it's right.. / Ross, I lost it again.
jokes.setup: Friends look at the sonogram photo and also can't find the baby.
jokes.punchline: Even as Rachel begins to show them, she loses sight of it again — 'Ross, I lost it again' — a final callback to the whole 'can't see the baby' arc.
jokes.explanation: A sweet, funny closing callback. 'Ross, I lost it again' mid-explanation is a good button on the sonogram arc — the callback extends the joke without overstaying its welcome.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh, so now you're attacking the way I eat? That's rich coming from you, Mr. I-Chew-Each-Bite-Forty-Times!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's called proper digestion, Rachel.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: It's called being boring! By the time you finish one plate, I've already had dessert and moved on with my life!

jokes.text: Second airport check-in attempt. Monica's plan works this time — they get bumped to first class. Chandler: 'See, if we'd gotten here earlier, those seats might not have been available. Compromise works.'
jokes.setup: Monica's plan of arriving on time (her way) finally works and they get first class
jokes.punchline: Chandler's completely revisionist 'Compromise works' — he's reframing Monica's victory as a joint triumph
jokes.explanation: Good payoff for the running gag — Chandler's forced concession disguised as wisdom. 'Compromise works' as a capitulation is very Chandler.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, maybe if you grew up with Monica, you'd understand that if you don't eat fast, you don't eat.

jokes.text: Monica: 'My name is Mrs. Bing. Haven't I compromised enough?'
jokes.setup: Chandler says 'compromise works' after Monica's approach wins
jokes.punchline: Monica's reminder that taking Chandler's name was itself a compromise — undercutting his self-congratulation
jokes.explanation: Very sharp line. 'Mrs. Bing' as a sacrifice is funny because 'Bing' is an objectively funny last name, and Monica calling it out as her own compromise is both character-specific and a clever reversal. High quotability, great economy. One of the episode's better lines.

dialogue.line: Doctor's polite understatement about obvious inappropriate situation

jokes.text: Monica removes an ankle bracelet at airport security. 'My anklet. That was a close one.'
jokes.setup: Monica and Chandler are going through airport security
jokes.punchline: Monica's total focus on her anklet as the security concern — treating a piece of jewelry as equivalent to a security threat
jokes.explanation: Light gag, Monica's vanity over security concerns. Mild joke, functions as setup bridge to the Chandler bomb joke. Not particularly inspired.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I'm the father.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: We're not together anymore.

jokes.text: Chandler reads the sign: 'Federal law prohibits any joking regarding aircraft hijacking or bombing.' Then: 'Don't worry about me, I take my bombs very seriously.'
jokes.setup: Chandler reads the airport security sign aloud
jokes.punchline: His immediate violation of the sign — 'I take my bombs very seriously' — a classic Chandler impulse to say the worst possible thing
jokes.explanation: Very Chandler — he compulsively says the thing the sign tells him not to. 'I take my bombs very seriously' is a good line. The setup is the sign itself. Strong character integration — Chandler's self-sabotaging anxiety manifesting as inappropriate humor is core to his personality.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Why won't you just admit that you need me?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I don't need you, Ross. I can stand on my own two feet.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not what I meant.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, during the exam, I was literally sitting down the whole time.

jokes.text: Chandler's interrogation: 'I know the sign says no jokes about bombs, but shouldn't the sign really say, No Bombs? Isn't that the guy we really have to worry about here? The guy with the bombs? Not the guy who jokes about his bombs?'
jokes.setup: Chandler is being questioned by security after his bomb jokes
jokes.punchline: His entirely reasonable-sounding (but completely wrong-read-room) semantic argument that the sign should address actual bombs, not bomb jokes
jokes.explanation: Chandler's internal logic is impeccable and completely insane — the argument is structurally sound (signs should address the real problem) while being catastrophically mistimed. 'Not the guy who jokes about his bombs' is a great line that also inadvertently confirms he jokes about bombs. The escalating self-entrapment is excellent character comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Look at that! That's our baby!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I can't see it.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'Not that I have bombs, but if I did, I probably wouldn't joke about them. I'd probably keep that rather quiet.'
jokes.setup: Chandler is still digging himself deeper with security
jokes.punchline: His hypothetical about what he would do if he actually had bombs — framed as reassurance but escalating the situation further
jokes.explanation: The crowning moment of the bomb sequence. 'Not that I have bombs, but if I did, I probably wouldn't joke about them. I'd keep that rather quiet' is perfectly constructed — each clause makes it worse than the last. The reassurance is itself incriminating. Very high quotability and character integration. Approaches the episode's best material.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You told the doctor you had maternal bonding with the baby?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, I didn't want him to think I was a bad mother!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So you lied to your doctor?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I was hormonal, Ross! I panic-bonded!

jokes.text: Monica, when asked her association with Chandler: 'He's my husband. Oh, but only for a few days. I don't know what he does outside of the house.'
jokes.setup: Security asks Monica about her connection to Chandler
jokes.punchline: Monica immediately throws Chandler under the bus by distancing herself — 'only for a few days' and 'I don't know what he does outside of the house' — implying she can't vouch for him
jokes.explanation: Monica's self-preservation instinct kicking in on her honeymoon is very true to character. 'Only for a few days' and the disclaimer about his outside activities are both sharp lines. Good complement to the Chandler escalation.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I lied! I'm not actually pregnant. I just wanted to see if you guys would still love me.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: And now I've failed as a mother before I even had a child. I'm the worst person alive.

jokes.text: Security asks what Chandler means by 'plan' (he's describing Monica's plan vs. his plan for airport timing). Chandler: 'You really should just ask me yes or no questions.'
jokes.setup: Security is questioning Chandler about his mention of 'her plan versus my plan'
jokes.punchline: Chandler's self-aware acknowledgment that his verbal filter is broken — advising them to constrain him to yes/no to prevent further self-incrimination
jokes.explanation: Meta-aware Chandler at his best — he knows his own problem and can diagnose it even as he's doing it. 'You should just ask me yes or no questions' is a great self-aware line. Very quotable and character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Can you see it now?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, I still can't see it.

jokes.text: Security goes through Chandler's bag — it's Monica's bag, packed perfectly with over 50 folded pieces. Monica: 'You're mean.'
jokes.setup: Security opens Chandler's bag and unpacks Monica's meticulously organized suitcase
jokes.punchline: Monica's devastated 'You're mean' at the security agent unpacking her 50+ perfectly folded items — her reaction is to the organizational destruction, not the security theater
jokes.explanation: Monica's obsessive organization making 'You're mean' the right response to a security search is good character comedy. The visual of 50 perfectly folded pieces being scattered is a strong visual gag implied by the dialogue. Character-specific and efficient.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Look, there's the baby. See the head right there?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, I see it! Oh wait... that's it?

jokes.text: Security clears them: 'All right, you're free to go.' Chandler: 'Thanks. About those Speedos, I don't know how they got in there.'
jokes.setup: Chandler is finally cleared by airport security
jokes.punchline: He raises the Speedo issue unprompted — referencing the opening of the episode and implying Monica packed them without telling him
jokes.explanation: Full-circle callback to the Speedo joke from the cold open — now it's revealed Monica packed them in Chandler's bag. The timing of raising it with security (right after being cleared) is good. Solid episode-closing callback. Rewatch bonus because the opening Speedo joke retroactively makes more sense.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: So the new lock is really secure? Because I was thinking about breaking in again for food.

jokes.text: Joey calls Monica: 'Phoebe and I smell gas coming from your apartment.' Chandler: 'Joey smells gas. What else is new?' (second time this joke appears in episode)
jokes.setup: Second instance of the Joey gas call (this is the actual call that happens in the B-plot timeline)
jokes.punchline: Same Chandler quip about Joey and gas — this is the actual call that Monica consents to breaking down the door
jokes.explanation: This appears to be the full version of the previously foreshadowed call. The gas/Joey joke repeats — slightly weakened by the second instance. The structure of the episode using this call twice is clever but the joke itself is at diminishing returns.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: We should show everyone the ultrasound picture.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I can't see it either.

jokes.text: You want us to break down your door? / Yes! / You won't blame us for any damage? / No! / You sure you want this? / No, I want you to just wait for the place to blow up.
jokes.setup: Joey proposes breaking down Monica's door (a third time, essentially repeating the earlier joke).
jokes.punchline: Monica's identical sarcastic response — 'No, I want you to just wait for the place to blow up' — echoes the earlier scene exactly, the repetition itself being the joke.
jokes.explanation: Third iteration of this joke — the diminishing returns are showing. The exact repetition works as a structural choice but isn't particularly fresh comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No, no, no, it's right there. See? Right there by the window.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Where? I don't see it.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Right there! By the curtain!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, I lost it again.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You just looked at it!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I know! I know where it was, and then I looked away for like two seconds...

tmdb_overview: Chandler and Monica prepare to leave for their honeymoon as Rachel prepares to tell Ross that he's the father of her baby. While traveling, Monica and Chandler become jealous of another honeymooning couple who get bumped to first class on the airplane. Meanwhile, Joey and Phoebe scheme to get inside the newlyweds' apartment after discovering that they don't have a key.
insight: Eighty-seven jokes in 22 minutes, but emotional weight drags humor impact below season average.
